previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was readmitted just five days after discharge due to worsening abdominal pain, constipation, and symptoms of a urinary tract infection. She had not had a bowel movement since her last discharge and reported chills and back pain. Evaluation revealed pyelonephritis caused by VRE, likely due to inadequate coverage with prior ciprofloxacin, and significant fecal loading contributing to abdominal discomfort. She was treated with IV ampicillin, transitioned to oral amoxicillin for a 14-day course, and an aggressive bowel regimen including oral and rectal laxatives and enemas, which led to symptom improvement. Her mental status stabilized with continued lactulose and rifaximin. She was discharged home with new prescriptions for senna and rectal bisacodyl, instructions to complete antibiotics, and referrals to follow up with gynecology for fibroids and monitor anemia.
